gaps.sentence: I'll take the job ___ they don't offer me any more money.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a future possibility that will not change the decision.

gaps.sentence: The flat is spacious and well located; ___, the rent is surprisingly low.
gaps.explanation: 'Moreover' adds another supporting point in the same direction.

gaps.sentence: ___ his impressive qualifications, he wasn't even shortlisted.
The plan was expensive; ___, the board approved it.
gaps.explanation: The approval happens in spite of the cost: nevertheless signals concession.

gaps.sentence: He had hardly stepped off the plane ___ he was rushed into a meeting.
I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: I noted down the reference number ___ I needed it later.
gaps.hint: just in case it proved necessary
gaps.explanation: 'In case' = because it might be needed later; no purpose is intended.

gaps.sentence: ___ the traffic was terrible, we arrived on time.
gaps.explanation: 'Although' introduces a clause with subject and verb. Despite/in spite of need a noun or -ing form.
